title: Then and now: the imperfect and the present perfect

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the *imperfecto* from B1 Unit 5, and the present perfect from A2 Unit 1, for change over time. The imperfect describes how things were before (*antes se hablaban…*, *no podían estudiar*); the present perfect links the past to today (*han creado programas*, *ha crecido*).

items.spanish: Antes de 1492 se hablaban cientos de lenguas en el continente.
items.english: Before 1492 hundreds of languages were spoken on the continent.

items.spanish: Muchos niños indígenas no podían estudiar en su lengua.
items.english: Many indigenous children could not study in their language.

items.spanish: En las últimas décadas, varios países han creado programas bilingües.
items.english: In recent decades, several countries have created bilingual programmes.

items.spanish: Se han publicado muchos libros en lenguas indígenas.
items.english: Many books have been published in indigenous languages.

sections.content: Use the imperfect with *antes*, *durante mucho tiempo* and *entonces*; use the present perfect with *en las últimas décadas*, *hasta ahora* and *todavía no*. The present perfect looks at a period that includes the present.
